## San Telmo excursions in Buenos Aires: what the routes include

[San Telmo](/argentina/place/san-telmo/) is one of the historic neighborhoods of [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/). Old facades, cobbled streets, cafés and antique shops survive here. The neighborhood's focal point is [Plaza Dorrego](/argentina/place/plaza-dorrego/), around which many walking routes pass.

We include San Telmo in **4 sightseeing excursions around the capital**. They offer different ways to discover the city; they are not four separate itineraries confined to San Telmo's streets. When choosing, consider what else is included, the stated guiding arrangements and how much time is devoted to the capital as a whole.

## Which excursions pass through San Telmo

| Excursion | Distinguishing feature |
|---|---|
| [Historic neighborhoods: private tour](/argentina/buenos-aires/buenos-aires-private-historic-neighbourhoods/) | Broad coverage of the city |
| [Historic neighborhoods with a Russian-speaking guide](/argentina/buenos-aires/buenos-aires-historic-districts-russian-private/) | Private, Russian-speaking guide |
| [Three-hour city tour](/argentina/buenos-aires/buenos-aires-three-hours-russian-group/) | Group tour, Russian-speaking guide |
| [City and parks](/argentina/buenos-aires/buenos-aires-city-parks-russian-private/) | Half-day tour, parks, Russian-speaking guide |

These options cover different parts of the capital and are not presented as dedicated walking tours of San Telmo alone. Their main routes also pass through other Buenos Aires neighborhoods.

## Historic San Telmo and Plaza Dorrego

San Telmo is ideal for exploring on foot: admire old houses' balconies, step into antique shops, notice details of the facades and stop at cafés. [Plaza Dorrego](/argentina/place/plaza-dorrego/) is surrounded by buildings connected with the history of old Buenos Aires.

On Sundays, the famous antiques fair usually takes place in the square and along nearby Defensa Street. On other days, the experience is different: the historic quarter remains interesting, but Sunday market trading cannot be promised on every excursion. Evening tango performances also require separate confirmation of dates and arrangements.

## Private excursion through the historic neighborhoods

The [private historic-neighborhoods tour](/argentina/buenos-aires/buenos-aires-private-historic-neighbourhoods/) combines San Telmo with [La Boca](/argentina/place/la-boca/), Plaza Dorrego, Plaza de Mayo, Casa Rosada, the Obelisk, Recoleta and Puerto Madero. It traces several eras of urban history, from old buildings and working-class neighborhoods to broad avenues and the redeveloped port.

The format is explicitly described as a **private excursion**. The guiding language and duration are not specified for this particular tour, so the conditions of neighboring programs should not be applied to it. A tango show with dinner is mentioned as a separate evening excursion.

## Historic neighborhoods with a Russian-speaking guide

The [private excursion with a Russian-speaking guide](/argentina/buenos-aires/buenos-aires-historic-districts-russian-private/) includes the Obelisk, La Boca, San Telmo, Plaza Dorrego, Plaza de Mayo and Casa Rosada.

This option suits travelers who want to hear the city's story in Russian and prefer a private format. San Telmo is combined with other landmark stops in the historic center, so travelers hoping for an unhurried exploration of antique shops should check how much time is allocated to the neighborhood.

## Three-hour group sightseeing excursion

The [Buenos Aires group sightseeing tour](/argentina/buenos-aires/buenos-aires-three-hours-russian-group/) lasts **3 hours**, takes place with a Russian-speaking guide and covers several well-known neighborhoods. Listed stops include San Telmo, La Boca, Plaza de Mayo, Recoleta and Puerto Madero.

This is an intensive introduction, with potentially brief stops. The excursion takes place **as part of a group within the tour itinerary**; an individual departure on the same terms should not be promised without confirmation. An evening tango show with dinner is arranged separately.

## Private itinerary including Lezama and Palermo parks

The [city-and-parks sightseeing tour](/argentina/buenos-aires/buenos-aires-city-parks-russian-private/) lasts **half a day**. A Russian-speaking guide introduces the historic neighborhoods, while the route also includes Parque Lezama and Parque Tres de Febrero in Palermo.

This itinerary connects San Telmo with a wider urban landscape of squares, avenues, modern Puerto Madero and green spaces. It suits travelers interested in history, architecture and city parks alike.

The services of a Russian-speaking guide are included. A tango show is treated as a separate program. Confirm the exact order of stops, the time spent walking through the neighborhood and access to building interiors before traveling.

## How to choose an excursion

If San Telmo is one of many sights you want to see on your first visit to the capital, the short [three-hour group tour](/argentina/buenos-aires/buenos-aires-three-hours-russian-group/) may suit you. For a private experience, compare the [historic-neighborhoods route](/argentina/buenos-aires/buenos-aires-historic-districts-russian-private/) with the [city-parks itinerary](/argentina/buenos-aires/buenos-aires-city-parks-russian-private/).

If antiques and the Sunday fair at Plaza Dorrego are your main goals, choose the date with the day of the week in mind and agree on time for walking in advance. Mentioning San Telmo on a general sightseeing tour does not guarantee a visit to the fair.

## Frequently asked questions about San Telmo excursions

### Can I see the Sunday fair at Plaza Dorrego?

Yes, if the excursion takes place when the fair is operating and the route allows time to visit. Sunday market trading is not automatically included in every sightseeing tour.

### Is there a tour with a Russian-speaking guide?

Yes. Russian-language guiding is expressly confirmed for the [private historic-neighborhoods route](/argentina/buenos-aires/buenos-aires-historic-districts-russian-private/), the [three-hour group excursion](/argentina/buenos-aires/buenos-aires-three-hours-russian-group/) and the [parks itinerary](/argentina/buenos-aires/buenos-aires-city-parks-russian-private/).

### Is an evening tango show included?

An evening tango show is offered separately from these daytime excursions. If you want to attend one, arrange it separately rather than assuming it forms part of a daytime San Telmo tour.

## Santa Susana Ranch excursion: a day of gaucho traditions

[Santa Susana Ranch](/argentina/place/santa-susana-ranch/) lies near Los Cardales in Buenos Aires Province. Travelers come here to discover rural Argentina: visit an estancia, enjoy the countryside, learn about gaucho culture and try a traditional barbecue lunch.

For this destination, we offer the [“Santa Susana Ranch: Gaucho Day with Argentine Lunch” excursion](/argentina/santa-susana-ranch/santa-susana-gaucho-day-lunch/). This is a **full-day program** with a guide, folklore entertainment, lunch and transfers as specified in the itinerary. It suits visitors who have already explored the city and want to discover a different side of Argentine life.

## What is an estancia, and why spend a day at one?

In Argentina, an estancia is a farm or rural estate. The history of such properties is closely connected with the pastures of the Pampas and the culture of gauchos, skilled horsemen and rural workers. Many country traditions survive in food, clothing, music and customs.

At Santa Susana, this introduction is organized as a full countryside excursion. The estancia atmosphere, traditional activities and a relaxed lunch are central to the experience. It contrasts with a walk through the historic neighborhoods of [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/): instead of museums and city streets, you spend the day outside the capital.

Our itinerary includes traditional activities and folklore entertainment. Check the specific performances and their order against the program for your chosen departure: visiting a ranch does not automatically mean that every possible horseback activity is included.

## Argentine lunch at the ranch

One of the day's highlights is Argentine barbecue. The tradition of *asado* has an important social role: meat is cooked over a fire, and sharing lunch becomes a distinct part of a countryside visit. Both the food and the time around the table matter on trips of this kind.

A **traditional lunch is included** in the [Ada Tours excursion to Santa Susana](/argentina/santa-susana-ranch/santa-susana-gaucho-day-lunch/). Drinks are paid for separately unless their inclusion has been agreed additionally. Discuss menus and special dietary requirements before the trip.

Travelers particularly interested in national cuisine and food traditions may also enjoy our selection of [food and wine tours in Argentina](/interests/food-and-wine/tours/argentina/) when suitable itineraries are available for the chosen dates.

## What the Ada Tours excursion includes

The program includes:

- a guided trip to Santa Susana Ranch;
- traditional activities and folklore entertainment as described in the itinerary;
- an Argentine barbecue lunch;
- transfers according to the itinerary.

The duration is stated as **a full day**. A single fixed price and a detailed schedule of every activity require separate confirmation. These should not be replaced with assumptions: the details of a particular departure are agreed when you choose the trip.

If you are comparing excursions during a stay in the capital, see the [Argentina excursions catalog](/argentina/excursion/) as well. Santa Susana is a rural cultural experience rather than a tour of city landmarks.

## Preparing for an estancia visit

Set aside the whole day for the ranch and allow for the drive from the Buenos Aires area. Closed shoes and comfortable casual clothing are practical in the countryside. In summer, bring sun protection and water; when temperatures fall, add an outer layer.

Weather in the province varies by season: summers are warm and winters cooler. Much of the experience takes place outdoors, so checking the forecast for your excursion day is worthwhile.

If you have a busy sightseeing schedule in the capital, plan the estancia on a separate day. That way, you will not need to rush back for an evening excursion, and the folklore program and lunch can be enjoyed in full.

## Frequently asked questions about Santa Susana excursions

### Can I visit Santa Susana for just a few hours?

Our excursion is designed as **a full-day experience**. A shorter outing would be a different product, with its route, meals and activities agreed separately.

### Are lunch and transfers included?

Yes. The [published excursion](/argentina/santa-susana-ranch/santa-susana-gaucho-day-lunch/) includes a traditional Argentine lunch and transfers according to the itinerary. Drinks are separate unless another arrangement is agreed in advance.

### Is this trip suitable for first-time visitors to Argentina?

Yes, especially if you want to discover gaucho customs and rural Argentine culture. You can set aside another day for your first introduction to Buenos Aires and keep Santa Susana as a separate countryside excursion.

## Gaucho Day at Santa Susana Ranch: how the excursion works

A trip to [Santa Susana Ranch](/argentina/place/santa-susana-ranch/) offers a full day away from [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) and an introduction to rural Argentina. The estancia is located in Buenos Aires Province near Los Cardales. The main experiences here revolve around gaucho traditions, a folklore program and a traditional Argentine barbecue lunch.

This excursion is intended for people interested in life on the Argentine Pampas and its cultural traditions. Our program includes a guide, transfers, traditional activities and entertainment, and lunch. **The duration is a full day.** The precise timetable of individual performances and stops depends on the agreed excursion program.

## What is an estancia, and why are gauchos central to its story?

In Argentina, an estancia is a farm or rural estate with surrounding land. Some are open to travelers. Unlike a city excursion through museums, an estancia introduces culture through the ranch environment, traditional food, music, clothing and horse-riding skills.

Gauchos have historically been connected with livestock farming on the Pampas plains. What makes a countryside day interesting is how familiar images of Argentina—vast pastures, horses and meat cooked over an open fire—come together in a single experience. However, a show for visitors and everyday farm work are different activities. The presentation of traditions remains an organized tourism program.

[Santa Susana](/argentina/place/santa-susana-ranch/) has its own history and specific location. It should not be confused with other estancias near the capital, even when several experiences have similar names such as “Fiesta Gaucha.”

## Lunch featuring Argentine barbecue

The Ada Tours excursion includes a traditional Argentine barbecue lunch. Its culinary centerpiece is *asado*, cooking meat over coals or an open flame, an important feature of family gatherings and social occasions in Argentina.

The meal has a different setting from a *parrilla* in the capital. At the estancia, lunch forms part of a day in the countryside, between discovering the property and enjoying the cultural program. In a city restaurant, the focus is usually on the menu, cooking methods and choice of venue. If you are particularly interested in a structured tasting of meats, desserts and wines, see the [Buenos Aires food tour](/argentina/buenos-aires/buenos-aires-food-tour/).

**Drinks are not automatically included in the basic description of the Santa Susana day:** they are paid for separately unless another arrangement is agreed. Do not assume that the menu and drinks promoted by the estancia itself are included in the specific Ada Tours product.

## Folklore and activities on the ranch

The program includes traditional activities and folklore entertainment. Such days at Argentine estancias may feature music, dancing, horsemen's performances and introductions to estate life. The exact activities vary by organizer and date.

Our excursion includes a cultural and entertainment component, but **a horseback ride for every guest, a particular museum, a performance by named artists or participation in competitions are not listed as separately guaranteed services**. If any of these matters especially to you, discuss it before confirming the excursion day.

On the [6-day Argentina tour that visits Santa Susana](/argentina/tour/argentina-experience-6-days/), the ranch has its own day. Travelers learn about the gauchos and have lunch at the estancia, then return for a farewell dinner at the hotel that evening according to the itinerary. This illustrates how a countryside outing can be combined with city sightseeing and other excursions.

## Planning the journey from Buenos Aires

The outing takes a full day, so it is wise not to schedule a substantial city sightseeing tour at the same time or a mandatory evening event immediately after the return. Travel time depends on your starting point and traffic leaving the city; it should be confirmed together with the transfer.

Closed shoes are useful for walking around the grounds. On warm days, bring water, sun protection and a hat; during cooler or windier periods, take an extra layer. Choose clothes for an open rural setting rather than for a restaurant dining room.

If your group includes children, older travelers or people with reduced mobility, ask in advance about walking distances and the conditions for participating in different activities. Having a transfer and a guide does not automatically mean that every activity is accessible without restrictions.

## Santa Susana, a food tour or a tango show: which should you choose?

These excursions explore different aspects of Argentine culture:

| Experience | Main attraction |
|---|---|
| Santa Susana | The Pampas, gauchos and a countryside lunch |
| Food tour | Restaurants, desserts and wines |
| Tango show | Stage dancing and dinner |

Choose a day at Santa Susana to discover rural traditions. To explore the capital's cuisine in greater depth, try the [food tour](/argentina/buenos-aires/buenos-aires-food-tour/). For an evening experience after city sightseeing, consider the [Tango Porteño dinner show](/argentina/buenos-aires/tango-porteno-dinner-show/). The products differ in duration, included services and format; none is a substitute for the others.

## Frequently asked questions about Santa Susana Ranch

### How long does the excursion last?

A full day is allocated to visiting the ranch. Exact departure and return times depend on the agreed itinerary and transfers.

### Is lunch included?

Yes. The Ada Tours excursion includes a traditional Argentine barbecue lunch. Drinks are paid for separately unless their inclusion has been agreed.

### Can I go horseback riding?

Such activities are offered at some Argentine estancias, but a separate ride for each participant is not confirmed as part of our excursion. Availability must be agreed separately.

### Can the ranch visit be included in a multi-day trip?

Yes. On the [“Argentina in 6 Days” itinerary](/argentina/tour/argentina-experience-6-days/), a visit to Santa Susana is already scheduled as its own day alongside Buenos Aires, Tigre and other experiences.

## Tours visiting Santa Susana Ranch in Argentina

A [gaucho day at Santa Susana Ranch](/argentina/santa-susana-ranch/santa-susana-gaucho-day-lunch/) is included in the [6-day “Argentina: Buenos Aires, Tigre and Gaucho Traditions” itinerary](/argentina/tour/argentina-experience-6-days/). Day five is devoted to the ranch. Guests discover rural traditions, enjoy folklore entertainment and an Argentine barbecue. The experience offers a view of Argentina beyond the capital's streets and familiar urban sightseeing.

The journey also includes [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), an evening of tango, [Tigre](/argentina/place/tigre/) and the Paraná Delta, and a day trip to [Colonia del Sacramento](/uruguay/place/colonia-del-sacramento/) in Uruguay. Argentina remains the principal country of the route, while the Uruguay visit is explicitly part of day four.

## Where the gaucho day falls in the six-day itinerary

| Day | Main activity |
|---|---|
| 1 | Arrival in Buenos Aires |
| 2 | City sightseeing and tango |
| 3 | Tigre and the Paraná Delta |
| 4 | Colonia del Sacramento |
| 5 | Santa Susana Ranch |
| 6 | Airport transfer |

The first days focus on urban history and culture. During the Buenos Aires sightseeing excursion, the itinerary includes a guide, lunch and a tango show. On the following day, canals and islands of the Paraná Delta replace the cityscape. The group then crosses the Río de la Plata by ferry to visit historic Colonia del Sacramento.

On day five, travelers head to [Santa Susana Ranch](/argentina/place/santa-susana-ranch/). The focus shifts to gaucho life: rural activities, horsemanship traditions, local folklore and the food of the Pampas. In the evening, the six-day itinerary includes a farewell dinner at the hotel.

This sequence makes the estancia day an experience in its own right, not a brief stop between city landmarks. A thorough introduction to Argentine ranches and riding culture would take more time: one excursion provides a first impression but does not replace a specialized horseback-riding trip.

## What the Santa Susana excursion includes

The stand-alone excursion includes a guide, transfers as specified in the program, traditional activities, folklore entertainment and an Argentine barbecue lunch. **Drinks are paid for separately**, unless their inclusion has been agreed.

Programs at different Argentine estancias can vary considerably. Do not automatically expect private riding lessons, a particular equestrian demonstration or unlimited drinks: these services are not specified for this product. For a corporate group, Ada Tours can agree on the visit sequence and necessary organizational details as part of a specific quotation.

Gauchos have historically been associated with livestock raising on the Argentine Pampas. Their horsemanship, musical traditions and rural way of life helped shape an unmistakable aspect of Argentine culture. A day at the ranch offers an opportunity to experience these traditions firsthand.

## A group tour versus a separate excursion day

The [6-day tour](/argentina/tour/argentina-experience-6-days/) is organized in a group format and is designed, among other audiences, for corporate travelers. Rates are calculated for specific group sizes and accommodation arrangements. An important condition is that **accommodation is not included in the base price unless agreed separately**. It would therefore be misleading to compare its price directly with a private tour in which hotels have already been paid for.

Groups should agree in advance on participant numbers, transport, meals and actual guiding requirements. Shortening or extending the program also changes the pricing arrangements. The stand-alone [Santa Susana excursion](/argentina/santa-susana-ranch/santa-susana-gaucho-day-lunch/) suits people already staying in the capital who want to devote one day to rural traditions.

Travelers considering a broader journey may find it helpful to compare [Argentina tours](/argentina/tour/) and [cultural itineraries around the country](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/argentina/). Pay attention to the actual number of excursions, meal inclusions and how prices are calculated, rather than duration alone.

## Frequently asked questions about Santa Susana Ranch tours

### On which day of the six-day tour is the ranch visited?

On day five. Before it, the itinerary includes Buenos Aires sightseeing, a trip to Tigre and a visit to Colonia del Sacramento.

### Is ranch lunch included?

Yes. A traditional Argentine barbecue lunch is specified. Drinks are included only if separately agreed.

### Is horseback riding guaranteed for every traveler?

No such condition appears in the approved description. Traditional activities and folklore entertainment are listed; specific individual activities are discussed separately.

### Is the program suitable for a corporate group?

Yes. The six-day itinerary uses a group format and includes corporate travelers among its intended audiences. Participant numbers, transfers and accommodation are determined at the quotation stage.

### Is Uruguay really part of the route?

Yes. Day four includes a journey to Colonia del Sacramento across the Río de la Plata and a return to Buenos Aires.

## Excursions to Tierra del Fuego National Park from Ushuaia

[Tierra del Fuego National Park](/argentina/place/tierra-del-fuego-national-park/) lies on the island of Tierra del Fuego, close to [Ushuaia](/argentina/place/ushuaia/). In one trip, you can experience subantarctic forests, mountains, cold lakes and sea bays. This is one of the parts of Patagonia where the Andes meet the coast.

To visit the park, we offer a [group excursion with an English-speaking guide](/argentina/ushuaia/tierra-del-fuego-english-group/). Its route brings together the Pipo River, Ensenada Zaratiegui Bay, Lake Roca (Acigami) and Lapataia Bay. It suits travelers who want to experience several different natural landscapes of southern Argentina in a relatively short time.

## Places included in the itinerary

The excursion starts in Ushuaia and travels through the national park. The program names several natural sites, each revealing a different side of Tierra del Fuego.

**Pipo River** flows among forests and mountain slopes. Mount Susana is also mentioned on the route. The contrast between the valley's dense vegetation and the rugged outlines of the surrounding mountains is striking.

**Ensenada Zaratiegui Bay** offers views across coastal waters toward Redonda Island. Its marine coastline distinguishes Tierra del Fuego from many other South American national parks: forests and sea inlets can be experienced in one excursion.

**Lake Roca, also called Acigami**, lies among mountain forests. Both names refer to the same lake in the Argentine section of the park; its waters extend toward the Chilean border.

**Lapataia Bay** is one of the best-known endpoints of road journeys through Tierra del Fuego. Visitors come for its calm water, coastal vegetation and views of distant mountain ranges.

The description of the [English-guided excursion](/argentina/ushuaia/tierra-del-fuego-english-group/) also mentions lagoons, a beaver dam and a woodland cabin. The exact order of stops depends on the confirmed departure program. Long independent trekking routes are not automatically part of this group excursion.

## Group format and guiding language

The confirmed Ada Tours option is a **group excursion with an English-speaking guide**. This is an important selection criterion: if you need commentary in Russian or a private pace, the conditions of another format should be agreed separately.

The inclusion of entrance tickets, meals and transfers in this group program requires separate confirmation. Do not assume they have automatically been paid for. Before booking, check the meeting point, order of stops, duration and entrance fees.

You can also consider the separate [“Tierra del Fuego National Park” excursion](/argentina/ushuaia/argentina-ushuaia-tierra-del-fuego-national-park/), which focuses on the park's natural scenery. The price is **$76 per person**, with a possible discount for multiple participants. The conditions of this other excursion should not be transferred to the English-guided group option: these are distinct offers.

## Weather, seasons and suitable clothing

Tierra del Fuego can be cool, windy and damp even when northern Argentina is warm. The weather can change quickly, and some parts of the route run along exposed shores. Bring a windproof jacket, a warm layer, comfortable non-slip shoes and rain protection.

In summer, long daylight hours help with planning nature outings. In winter, cold, snow and road conditions call for greater care. Access to the park is via Ruta Nacional 3, and some roads within it are unpaved. Check the condition of the route and access to particular stops for your chosen date.

Walking enthusiasts should distinguish a sightseeing tour from independent trekking. The park has trails of varying difficulty, but their presence does not mean they will be covered as part of the selected excursion. For a more active trip, browse [adventure tours in Argentina](/interests/adventure/tours/argentina/).

## Adding a park visit to a longer journey

The park is most conveniently visited from Ushuaia, with a dedicated portion of the itinerary set aside for it. Driving and sightseeing stops take time, particularly in changeable weather. Avoid scheduling the excursion too close to a flight: road delays or itinerary changes could leave too little time for the airport.

If your journey also includes other parts of [Argentina](/argentina/), prepare for the climate differences. Clothes suitable for Buenos Aires or Iguazú will not replace appropriate gear for Tierra del Fuego. Layers and waterproof outerwear are useful in the south.

## Frequently asked questions about Tierra del Fuego excursions

### Where does the park excursion start?

For the [Ada Tours group option](/argentina/ushuaia/tierra-del-fuego-english-group/), Ushuaia is the departure city. Confirm the exact meeting point and transfer conditions in the approved itinerary.

### Where does Lapataia Bay appear in the program?

Lapataia is one of the listed natural stops on the group excursion, alongside the Pipo River, Ensenada Zaratiegui Bay and Lake Roca. The order of visits may depend on departure conditions.

### Is special preparation needed?

For a sightseeing excursion, warm waterproof clothing and comfortable shoes are the main essentials. If you plan a separate long trek, fitness and route requirements will be different.
